text.p: Nationsbank Corp. said Tuesday it completed the $9.8 billion acquisition of Boatmen's Bancshares after the U.S. Supreme Court refused to block a move to keep the deal from going through.
The closing creates the nation's fourth-largest banking company with assets of about $225 billion as of Sept. 30, NationsBank said.

On Monday, the U.S. Supreme Court refused to block NationsBank's acquisition of Boatmen's Bancshares. Justice Stephen Breyer denied a request for an emergency stay order from two community groups that opposed the transaction.
Friday, a U.S. Court of Appeals in Denver denied a stay sought by the two groups, InnerCity Press/Community on the Move and the New Mexico Alliance, to stop the acquisition.

The groups argued bank customers would be harmed by the merger of St. Louis-based Boatmen's with NationsBank, based in Charlotte, N.C. They said the acquisition would result in bank closings and higher ATM fees.

NationsBank now has franchises in 16 states -- Arkansas, Florida, Georgia, Illinois, Iowa, Kansas, Kentucky, Maryland, Missouri, New Mexico, North Carolina, Oklahoma, South Carolina, Tennessee, Texas and Virginia -- and the District of Columbia.
NationsBank stock was down 50 cents at $98.25 on the New York Stock Exchange in early afternoon trading.
